articles.title: पूर्वी नाकाबाट विदेशी पर्यटक बढे, सबैभन्दा धेरै भुटानी
articles.summary:
झापा । पूर्वी नेपालको प्रमुख स्थलमार्ग काँकरभिट्टा नाका हुँदै आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२\८३ मा ८६ देशका ९ हजार ४४७ जना विदेशी पर्यटक नेपाल भित्रिएका छन्। अध्यागमन कार्यालय काँकरभिट्टाको तथ्याङ्कअनुसार यो संख्या दैनिक औसत करिब २६ जना विदेशी पर्यटक नेपाल प्रवेश गरेको हो ।

आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२\८३ मा काँकरभिट्टा नाकाबाट नेपाल प्रवेश गर्ने विदेशी पर्यटकमा भुटान, अमेरिका, थाइल्याण्ड, अष्ट्रेलिया, बेलायत, क्यानडा, जर्मनी, फ्रान्स, जापान र रुसलगायत देशका नागरिक छन् । कुल आगन्तुकमध्ये भुटानी नागरिकको हिस्सा सबैभन्दा ठूलो छ । ४ हजार ९९४ जना भुटानी नागरिक नेपाल प्रवेश गरेका छन् ।

जुन कुल पर्यटक संख्याको करिब ५३ प्रतिशत हो । त्यस्तै २ हजार १५२ जना अमेरिकी नागरिकले काँकरभिट्टा नाका हुँदै नेपाल प्रवेश गरेका छन् । यो कुल आगन्तुकको करिब २३ प्रतिशत हो । भारतका नागरिकलाई नेपाल प्रवेश गर्न भिसा आवश्यक नपर्ने भएकाले उनीहरूलाई तेस्रो मुलुकका पर्यटकसम्बन्धी तथ्याङ्कमा समावेश गरिएको छैन ।

महिनागत तथ्याङ्कअनुसार सबैभन्दा बढी विदेशी पर्यटक पुसमा १ हजार ८५० जना र सबैभन्दा कम भदौमा २१६ जना नेपाल प्रवेश गरेका छन् । अध्यागमन कार्यालयले पुस र माघलाई प्रमुख पर्यटकीय याम मानेको छ ।

पर्यटकको आगमन उत्साहजनक भएपनि बसाइ छोटो हुने गरेको होटल व्यवसायी बताउँछन। पूर्वी नेपालका पर्यटकीय गन्तव्यमा पर्यटकलाई केही दिन रोक्न सके झापा, इलाम, ताप्लेजुङलगायत जिल्लाको पर्यटन तथा होटल व्यवसायमा उल्लेख्य योगदान पुग्ने उनीहरूको भनाइ छ ।

पूर्वी नेपालका पर्यटकीय गन्तव्यको अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय प्रचारप्रसार र सीमा नाकामै यातायात, होटल तथा भ्रमणसम्बन्धी सूचना उपलब्ध गराउनुपर्ने पर्यटन व्यवसायी कुन्दन निरौला बताउँछन् ।

अध्यागमन कार्यालय काँकरभिट्टाले सन् २०२४ अगस्टदेखि पूर्ण रूपमा अध्यागमन सेवा सञ्चालन गरेको थियो । सेवा प्रभावकारी भएपछि विदेशी पर्यटकको आगमन क्रमशः बढेको सूचना अधिकारी इन्द्रकुमार राजवंशी बताउँछन् ।

अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय प्रचारप्रसार, पर्यटन सूचना केन्द्र र आकर्षक प्याकेज निर्माणसँगै संघ, प्रदेश र स्थानीय तहबीच समन्वय गर्न सके विदेशी पर्यटकको संख्या बढाउन सकिने देखिन्छ । यसबाट होटल, यातायात, ट्राभल्स, हस्तकला तथा स्थानीय उत्पादनको बजारसमेत लाभान्वित हुने देखिएको छ ।

articles.title: राँगाको सिङबाट बन्ने गुँला पर्वको मुख्य बाजा !
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेवार समुदायका विशेषगरी बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बीको प्रमुख सांस्कृतिक पर्व गुँला बिहीबारदेखि सुरु भएको छ । एक महिनासम्म मनाइने पर्वमा भक्तजनले परम्परागत बाजागाजासहित चैत्य, विहार र मन्दिरको परिक्रमा गर्दै बुद्धको पूजा–आराधना गर्ने गर्दछन् ।

काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका परम्परागत नेवार वस्ती र टोलहरुमा अब एक महिनासम्म सडक वा गल्लीहरुमा विहान मानिसहरुको चहलपहल शुरु नहुँदै सुनिने छ, धिमे, भुस्या, बाँसुरी र न्याकुँको सुमधुर आवाज । अनि बाजाको यही धुन पछ्याउँदै मानिसहरू चैत्यतर्फ अघि बढिरहेका हुने छन् । यो गुँला पर्वको अवसरमा देखिने दृश्य हो ।

नेवार समुदायमा पनि विशेषगरी बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बीले मनाउने गुँला पर्व बिहीबारदेखि सुरु भएको छ । श्रावण शुक्ल प्रतिपदादेखि भाद्र शुक्ल प्रतिपदासम्म चल्ने यो पर्व करिब एक महिनासम्म धार्मिक र सांस्कृतिक गतिविधिले उपत्यकालाई जीवन्त बनाउँछ ।

गुँला शब्दको अर्थ आफैमा रोचक पनि छ । नेपाल भाषामा ‘गुँ’ को अर्थ नौ र ‘ला’ को अर्थ महिना भन्ने गरिन्छ । नेपाल संवतको नवौँ महिनामा मनाइने भएकाले यसको नाम गुँला रहन गएको मानिन्छ । गुँलाको वास्तविक आकर्षण बिहानै सुरु हुने यात्रामा देखिन्छ । भक्तजनहरू परम्परागत बाजा बजाउँदै विभिन्न चैत्य, विहार, बहाः र बहीको परिक्रमा गर्छन् ।

काठमाडौंको स्वयम्भू, बौद्ध, पाटनलगायतका धार्मिक तथा ऐतिहासिक स्थलमा गुँला पर्वको विशेष रौनक देखिन्छ । एउटा समूह धिमे बजाउँदै अघि बढिरहेको हुन्छ । यसमा कसैले भुस्या बजाइरहेको हुन्छ भने कसैले न्याकुँको गहिरो आवाज निकालिरहेको हुन्छ । यही दृश्यले गुँलालाई काठमाडौँका अन्य धेरै जात्रा र पर्वहरुभन्दा फरक बनाएको छ ।

गुँला पूजा र परिक्रमा गर्ने पर्व मात्रै होइन । संगीत जोडिएको उपत्यकाको जीवित संस्कृति पनि हो । विशेषगरी न्याकुँ बाजा गुँलाको पहिचानसँग जोडिएको छ । राँगाको सिङबाट बनाइने यो बाजा हेर्दा साधारण देखिए पनि यसको ध्वनि निकै विशिष्ट हुन्छ ।

परम्परागत रूपमा धार्मिक यात्राहरुमा यसको प्रयोग हुँदै आएको छ । त्यसैगरी धिमे, बाँसुरी, भुस्या र धाः लगायतका बाजासँगै बज्दा यी आवाजले पनि गुँला पर्वमा सांगीतिक समूहको स्वरूप लिन्छन् । पछिल्लो समय यस्ता जात्रा पर्वमा नयाँ पुस्ताको सहभागिता पनि बढिरहेको छ । नयाँ पूस्ताको सहभागितासँगै परम्परागत पर्व र संस्कृति पुस्तान्तरण पनि हुँदैछन् ।

गुँला धार्मिक पर्व मात्रैमा सीमित छैन । सामाजिकरुपमा खेतीपातीको मुख्य काम सकिएको समयसँग पनि यो पर्व जोडिएको छ । मानिसहरू केही फुर्सदिला हुने यही समयमा समुदाय भेला हुने, भेटघाट गर्ने र सामूहिक रूपमा धार्मिक गतिविधिमा सहभागी हुने अवसर पनि गुँलाले जुटाइ दिएको छ ।

बौद्ध परम्परामा वर्षायामको साधना र धार्मिक अभ्याससँग पनि गुँला समयको सम्बन्ध जोडिन्छ । त्यसैले यो अवधि पूजा, ध्यान, पाठ, दान र पुण्यकर्मका लागि विशेष मानिन्छ । यसको अर्को पक्ष के भने गुँला पर्वमा हुने चैत्य परिक्रमा एउटा यात्रा मात्रै होइन ।

उपत्यकाका विभिन्न स्थानीय धार्मिक स्थललाई जोड्ने सांस्कृतिक नेटवर्क जस्तो पनि हो । एउटा टोलबाट अर्को टोल, एउटा बहाःबाट अर्को चैत्यसम्म बाजाको धुनले यी ठाउँहरूलाई जोडिरहेको हुन्छ । काठमाडौंलाई मन्दिरै–मन्दिरको सहर भनिन्छ । तर गुँला पर्वले कामठाडौँ बाजा, बहाः, बही र चैत्यहरूको पनि सहर हो भन्ने प्रमाण पनि दिन्छ । एक महिनासम्म बज्ने यी बाजाहरु पुर्खाको स्मृति हुन्, धार्मिक आस्था हुन् र पहिचानको आवाज हुन् ।

articles.title: काठमाडौंमा पोर्चुगल कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापना गर्ने निर्णयकाे एनआरएनएद्वारा स्वागत
articles.summary:
काठमाडाैँ । काठमाडौंमा पोर्चुगल कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापना गर्ने निर्णय गरेपछि गैरआवासीय नेपाली संघ (एनआरएनए) पोर्चुगलले उक्त निर्णयको स्वागत गर्दै नेपाल तथा पोर्चुगल सरकारप्रति आभार व्यक्त गरेको छ।

नेपाल सरकारको २०८३ साउन २६ गते बसेको मन्त्रिपरिषद् बैठकले पोर्चुगल सरकारलाई काठमाडौंमा कन्सुलर कार्यालय खोल्न सहमति दिने निर्णय गरेको थियो। निकट भविष्यमा नै कार्यालय सञ्चालनमा आउने अपेक्षा गरिएको एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलले जनाएको छ।

एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलका अध्यक्ष सुजन लामा मोक्तानले जारी गरेको विज्ञप्तिमा काठमाडौंमै पोर्चुगलको कन्सुलर कार्यालय सञ्चालनमा आएपछि पोर्चुगलमा रहेका नेपालीलाई विभिन्न कन्सुलर सेवा लिन सहज हुने उल्लेख गरिएको छ। विशेषगरी पारिवारिक पुनर्मिलन, भिसा तथा अन्य कन्सुलर सेवाका लागि हाल भारतको नयाँ दिल्लीसम्म पुग्नुपर्ने बाध्यता कम हुने संघको विश्वास छ।

नयाँ सरकार गठन भएपछि काठमाडौंमा पोर्चुगलको कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापनाका लागि नेपाल सरकारको तर्फबाट आवश्यक पहल अघि बढाइएको थियो। सोही क्रममा परराष्ट्रमन्त्री शिशिर खनालले पोर्चुगलका राज्य तथा विदेश मामिलामन्त्री पाउलो राङ्गेलसँग टेलिफोन संवाद गरी कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापनालगायतका विषयमा कुराकानी गरेका थिए।

नेपाल सरकारको अनुरोध तथा त्यसपछिका कूटनीतिक पहलपछि पोर्चुगल सरकारले काठमाडौंमा कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापना गर्ने निर्णय गरेको हो। एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलले यसलाई पोर्चुगलमा रहेका नेपाली समुदायका लागि महत्वपूर्ण उपलब्धिका रूपमा लिएको छ।

नेपाल र पोर्चुगलबीच १ सेप्टेम्बर १९७६ मा औपचारिक कूटनीतिक सम्बन्ध स्थापना भएको थियो। लामो समयसम्म नेपालले पोर्चुगलमा आवासीय दूतावास स्थापना नगरेका कारण पोर्चुगलसम्बन्धी नेपाली कूटनीतिक जिम्मेवारी पेरिसस्थित नेपाली दूतावासले सम्हाल्दै आएको थियो।

नेपाल सरकारले सन् २०२५ मार्चमा लिस्बनमा आवासीय नेपाली राजदूतावास स्थापना गरेको थियो। लिस्बनमा स्थापना भएको नेपाली दूतावासका पहिलो आवासीय राजदूत प्रकाशमणि पौडेल हुन्।

दूतावासको औपचारिक उद्घाटन भने २० फेब्रुअरी २०२६ मा परराष्ट्र सचिव अमृतबहादुर रायको पोर्चुगल भ्रमणका क्रममा गरिएको थियो। यससँगै नेपाल–पोर्चुगल सम्बन्ध थप संस्थागत र प्रत्यक्ष बनेको एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलको भनाइ छ।

पोर्चुगलमा नेपालीको यकिन तथ्यांक नभए पनि ६० हजारभन्दा बढी नेपाली रहेको अनुमान नेपाली दूतावासले गरेको छ। ठूलो संख्यामा नेपाली समुदाय रहेको पोर्चुगलका लागि काठमाडौंमै पोर्चुगलको कन्सुलर सेवा सुरु हुनु महत्वपूर्ण कदम भएको एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलले जनाएको छ।

काठमाडौंमा कन्सुलर कार्यालय सञ्चालनमा आएपछि पोर्चुगलमा रहेका नेपालीले सेवा लिन भारतको नयाँ दिल्लीसम्म पुग्नुपर्ने अवस्थाको अन्त्य हुने तथा समय र आर्थिक खर्चसमेत बचत हुने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

articles.title: अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय युवा दिवसको अवसरमा सरसफाइ कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय युवा दिवसको अवसरमा रोटरी क्लब अफ गोंगबु र रोट्रयाक्ट क्लब अफ गोंगबु नर्थको संयुक्त आयोजनामा गरिएको तारकेश्वर–६ स्थित महांकाल मन्दिर क्षेत्रमा सरसफाइ कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न भएको छ ।

बुधबार बिहान ७ः३० बजेदेखि सञ्चालन गरिएको कार्यक्रममा ३५ जना रोटेरियन तथा रोट्रयाक्ट सदस्यहरूको सहभागिता रहेको थियो। सहभागीहरूले मन्दिर परिसर तथा आसपासका क्षेत्रमा सरसफाइ गर्दै फोहोर व्यवस्थापन र स्वच्छ वातावरण निर्माणसम्बन्धी जनचेतना फैलाएका छन् ।

कार्यक्रमले सार्वजनिक स्थलको स्वच्छता कायम राख्नुका साथै युवाहरूलाई सामाजिक सेवामा सक्रिय रूपमा सहभागी गराउने उद्देश्य राखेको आयोजकले जनाएको छ ।

रोटरीको Create Lasting Impact भन्ने मूल भावनाअनुसार आयोजित कार्यक्रममा सहभागीहरूले समुदायको विकास र वातावरण संरक्षणका लागि यस्ता सामाजिक अभियानलाई निरन्तरता दिनुपर्नेमा जोड दिएका छन् ।

रोटरी क्लब अफ गोंगबु र रोट्रयाक्ट क्लब अफ गोंगबु नर्थले आगामी दिनमा पनि समुदाय केन्द्रित विभिन्न सामाजिक तथा वातावरणीय कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन गर्ने जनाएको छ ।

articles.title: आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सद्वारा कर्णालीकी छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई शैक्षिक छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्स लिमिटेडले कर्णाली प्रदेशबाट काठमाडौं आई जोरपाटीस्थित चामुण्डा माध्यमिक विद्यालय कक्षा १२ मा अध्ययनरत छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई शैक्षिक छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गरेको छ । शिक्षाको माध्यमबाट विद्यार्थीको क्षमता विकास तथा उज्ज्वल भविष्य निर्माणमा सहयोग पु¥याउने उद्देश्यले आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सले छात्रा शीता शाहीलाई छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गरेको हो । आफ्नो जन्मस्थान कर्णाली प्रदेश भए पनि काठमाडौंमा रही अध्ययन गर्दै आएकी शीता शाहीलाई प्रदान गरिएको यस सहयोगले उनको शैक्षिक यात्रालाई थप सहज बनाउँदै उच्च शिक्षा तथा आगामी लक्ष्यतर्फ अघि बढ्न प्रेरणा प्रदान गर्ने विश्वास फाइनान्सले लिएको छ ।

छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गर्दै आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सले छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई उज्ज्वल भविष्यका लागि हार्दिक बधाई तथा शुभकामना व्यक्त गरेको छ । साथै, आगामी दिनमा पनि अध्ययनमा निरन्तर मेहनत, लगनशीलता र समर्पणका साथ अघि बढ्दै उत्कृष्ट सफलता हासिल गर्न प्रोत्साहित गरेको छ ।

उक्त छात्रवृत्ति वितरण कार्यक्रमा आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सका प्रबन्धक अच्युत पण्डित, बौद्ध शाखा प्रबन्धक अजय राज रेग्मी, बजार व्यवस्थापन प्रमुख सञ्जोक गुरुङ तथा बजार व्यवस्थापन अधिकृत सरिना श्रेष्ठ लगायत चामुण्डा माध्यमिक विद्यालयका प्रधानाध्यापक तथा शिक्षकहरू र सामाजिक अभियान्ता टेक राज शाहीको उपस्थितिमा सम्पन्न भएको थियो।

आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्स लिमिटेडले आफ्नो सामाजिक उत्तरदायित्व (CSR) अन्तर्गत शिक्षा क्षेत्रलाई प्राथमिकतामा राख्दै आर्थिक तथा सामाजिक रूपमा सहयोगको आवश्यकता भएका विद्यार्थीको शैक्षिक विकासमा योगदान पु¥याउँदै आएको छ। कम्पनीले आगामी दिनमा पनि शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य तथा अन्य सामाजिक क्षेत्रमा आफ्नो सामाजिक उत्तरदायित्वलाई निरन्तरता दिने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरेको छ ।

articles.title: भृकुटीमण्डपमा नयाँ गाडी र बाइकको मेला, इभीमा सबैको आकर्षण
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । काठमाडौंको भृकुटीमण्डपमा मंगलबारदेखि नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो २०२६ सुरु भएको छ । ५५ वटा ब्रान्ड सहभागी यो एक्स्पोमा ४० भन्दा बढी नयाँ मोडलका सवारीसाधन प्रदर्शन गरिएका छन् ।

अटोप्रेमीहरूका लागि नयाँ गाडी खरिद गर्ने र नयाँ अपडेट बुझ्ने अवसर एक्स्पोले जुराएको छ । काठमाडौंको भृकुटीमण्डप अहिले नयाँ मोडलका गाडी, मोटरसाइकल र अत्याधुनिक मोबिलिटी प्रविधिले भरिएको छ । र, यो माहोलको अवसर नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो २०२६ ले जुटाएको हो । नेपाल अटोमोबाइल इम्पोर्टर्स एण्ड म्यानुफ्याक्चरर्स एशोसिएसन अर्थात् नाइमाले दोस्रोपटक आयोजना गरेको एक्स्पो मंगलबारदेखि सुरु भएको छ ।

नेपाल प्रहरीका महानिरीक्षक दानबहादुर कार्की र नाइमाकी अध्यक्ष ऋतुसिंह वैद्यले पानसमा बत्ती बालेर एक्स्पोको औपचारिक शुभारम्भ गरे । यसपटकको एक्स्पोमा ५५ वटा ब्राण्ड सहभागी छन् । जसमा ४० भन्दा बढी नयाँ मोडलका सवारीसाधन सार्वजनिक तथा प्रदर्शन गरिँदैछन् ।

नयाँ गाडी वा बाइक किन्ने सोचमा रहेकाहरुलाई भृकुटीमण्डपमा जारी एक्स्पो उत्कृष्ट गन्तव्य हुन सक्छ । एक्स्पोमा चारपांग्रेतर्फ हुन्डाई, टाटा, टोयोटा, महिन्द्रा, किया, निसान, बीवाईडी, एमजी, सिट्रोन, ओमोडा एन्ड जेको, डेन्जा, जिकर, लीपमोटर, वुलिङ, ग्रेट वाल मोटर्सलगायतका ब्राण्ड सहभागी छन् ।

त्यसैगरी दुईपांग्रेतर्फ बजाज, होन्डा, टीभीएस, रोयल इन्फिल्ड, केटीएम, सुजुकी, एथर, याडिया, अल्ट्राभायोलेट, सीएफ मोटो, ट्रायम्फलगायतका ब्राण्डले आफ्ना नयाँ उत्पादन प्रदर्शनीमा राखेका छन् ।

कमर्सियल भेहिकलतर्फ पनि चेरी वान्डा, केरी, डोङफेङ, स्काइवर्थलगायतका ब्राण्डका गाडीहरु एक्स्पोमा देख्न सकिन्छ । एक्स्पोको अर्को आकर्षणमा रुपमा यहाँ रहेका स्टलहरु र छुट अफर रहेको छ । ग्राहकलाई आकर्षित गर्न कम्पनीहरूले आकर्षक तथा फरक शैलीका स्टल निर्माण गरेका छन् । विभिन्न ब्राण्डले विशेष छुट र अफरसमेत सार्वजनिक गरिरहेका छन् ।

नाइमाकी अध्यक्ष ऋतु सिंह वैद्यका अनुसार नेपालको अटोमोबाइल क्षेत्र विस्तारै विद्युतीय सवारीतर्फ अघि बढिरहेको छ । विद्युतीय सवारीले हरित अर्थतन्त्र निर्माणमा योगदान पु¥याइरहेको उनको भनाइ छ । उनले नेपालमा अटो कम्पोनेन्ट उद्योगलाई प्रोत्साहन गर्न सके एसेम्बल प्लान्टको सम्भावना अझ बलियो हुने बताएकी छन् ।

एक्स्पोमा सवारीसाधनसँगै बैंक तथा वित्तीय संस्था र बीमा कम्पनीको सहभागिता छ भने विभिन्न नलेज सिरिज पनि सञ्चालन भइरहेका छन् । नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो साउन ३१ गतेसम्म सञ्चालन हुनेछ ।

articles.title: घण्टाकर्णका आतंक र अन्त्यको कथा गथाँमुगः पर्व
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका नेवार समुदायले मंगलवार घण्टाकर्ण अर्थात् गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाएका छन् । घण्टाकर्ण दानवको अन्त्य गरिएको स्मरणमा मनाइने यो पर्वमा तीनखुट्टे राक्षसको आकृति बनाएर साँझ आगोमा जलाउँदै भूतप्रेत, रोगव्याधि र नकारात्मक शक्ति भगाउने परम्परा छ । गथाँमुगःको अवसरमा काठमाडौं, भक्तपुर र ललितपुरमा यो पर्वको विशेष रौनक देखियो ।

प्रत्येक वर्ष श्रावण कृष्ण चतुर्दशीका दिन काठमाडौंका गल्ली, चोक र दोबाटोमा नरकट, छ्वाली र काठबाट एउटा अनौठो राक्षसी आकृति ठड्याइन्छ । त्यसका तीनवटा खुट्टा हुन्छन् । शरीर विशाल छ । अनि साँझ परेपछि त्यही आकृतिलाई टोलवासीले घिसार्दै दोबाटोसम्म पु¥याउँछन् र आगो लगाएर जलाउँछन् । काठमाडौँमा वर्सेनि देखिने यो दृश्य गथाँमुगः पर्वको हो । गथाँमुगः पर्व अहिले गैर नेवार समुदायबीच गठेमंगलको नामले परिचित भइरहेको छ । गथाँमुगः काठमाडौं उपत्यकाको नेवार समुदायको महत्वपूर्ण सांस्कृतिक पर्व हो ।

यो पर्वसँग जोडिएको एउटा सबैभन्दा चर्चित किंवदन्ति छ । जुन घण्टाकर्ण नाम गरेको अत्याचारी राक्षससँग सम्बन्धित रहेको छ । किंवदन्ती अनुसार घण्टाकर्ण यति ठूलो अत्याचारी थियो कि बाटो हिँड्ने मानिससँग जबर्जस्ती कर उठाउँथ्यो, दुःख दिन्थ्यो र समाजलाई आतंकित बनाएको थियो । धार्मिक मन्त्र वा पवित्र कुरा सुन्न उसलाई मनै पर्दैन थियो । त्यसैले यस्ता कुरा सुन्न नपरोस् भनेर उसले आफ्ना दुवै कानमा ठूला घण्टा झुन्ड्याएको थियो ।

जब उ हिड्थ्यो ती घण्टा ठूलो आवाज निकालेर बज्थे । त्यसैले उसको नाम नै घण्टाकर्ण रहन गएको विश्वास गरिन्छ । तर यो किंवदन्तिमा पनि ट्वीस्ट आउँछ । एकदिन अत्याचारी घण्टाकर्णको अन्त्य हुन्छ । एक दिन एक चतुर तान्त्रिकले घण्टाकर्णलाई छलपूर्वक दलदलमा फसाउने योजना बनाउँछन् । राक्षस दलदलमा नराम्ररी फस्छ । निस्कन नसकेपछि वर्षौंदेखि उसको आतंक सहिरहेका मानिसहरूले ढुंगा र माटो प्रहार गरेर उसको अन्त्य गरिदिन्छन् । यही सामूहिक विजयको सम्झना र खुशीयालीमा गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाउने परम्परा शुरु भएको जनविश्वास रहेको छ । त्यसैले हरेक वर्ष श्रावण कृष्ण चतुर्दशीका दिन काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका नेवार समुदायमा गथाँमुगःको बेग्लै रौनक शुरु हुन्छ । काठमाडौं होस्, भक्तपुर होस् वा ललितपु, टोलटोलमा यसको छुट्टै चहलपहल देखिन्छ । घरका ढोकामा फलामको औंठी वा अन्य सुरक्षात्मक वस्तु राख्ने, घर सफा गर्ने, चोकमा राक्षसको आकृति बनाउने तथा विभिन्न परम्परागत विधि पूरा गर्ने चलन छ । कतिपय स्थानमा बालबालिका र युवाहरू घरघरमा गएर सहयोग वा दान संकलन गर्छन् ।

कतै परम्परागत गीत, बाजागाजा र सांस्कृतिक गतिविधिले उपत्यकाको वातावरणलाई थप जीवन्त र सांस्कृतिक बनाउँछ । यो पर्व मनाउने क्रममा दिनभर तयार गरिएको घण्टाकर्णको प्रतीकात्मक आकृतिलाई साँझतिर टोलवासी मिलेर तानेर दोबाटोसम्म पु¥याउँछन् । त्यसपछि विधिपूर्वक त्यसलाई जलाइन्छ । यसरी जलाइएको घण्टाकर्णको प्रतिक पर्वको निरन्तरताको रुपमा मात्रै रहेको छैन । यसको सांकेतिक अर्थ खराब शक्तिमाथि असल शक्तिको विजयको प्रतीक पनि हो । रोगव्याधि, भूतप्रेत, अशुभ शक्ति र नकारात्मक ऊर्जा घर तथा समाजबाट टाढा जाओस् भन्ने धार्मिक विश्वास पनि यो पर्वसँग जोडिएको छ । गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाउने क्रममा काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका टोल बस्तीहरूमा यसको आफ्नै स्थानीय शैली र परम्परा भेटिन्छ ।

काठमाडौंका पुराना नेवारी टोलदेखि भक्तपुरका ऐतिहासिक बस्ती र ललितपुरका परम्परागत चोकसम्म गथाँमुगःले उपत्यकाको साझा सांस्कृतिक सम्पदालाई जिवित राखेको छ । आजको आधुनिक काठमाडौँमा इन्टरनेट, मोबाइल, सामाजिक सञ्जाल र व्यस्त जीवनशैलीबीच पनि अमूल्य निधिका रुपमा रहेका यस्ता जात्रा तथा पर्वहरुले निरन्तरता पाइरहेका छन् । त्यसैले हरेक जात्रा वा पर्वजस्तै गथाँमुगःको दिन साँझपख काठमाडौँका नेवारी वस्ती वा चोकमा घण्टाकर्णको आकृति आगोमा जलिरहेको देख्न पाइन्छ । यही कारण सयौँ वर्ष पुरानो यो परम्परा आज पनि काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका गल्ली गल्लीमा उस्तै जीवन्त छ ।

articles.title: राडारमा गंगा, भानु र प्रकाश, देउवा–प्रचण्डका स्वकीयविरुद्ध अख्तियारको अनुसन्धान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । अख्तियार सक्रिय बनेको छ। स–साना मुद्दामा अल्झिने गरेको अख्तियार पछिल्लो समय ठूला भनिएकाहरुसम्म पुग्ने प्रयास गरिरहेको छ। रत, अख्तियारले चालेका यस्ता कदमहरु कति सफल वा असफल त्यसको लेखाजोखा छुट्टे होला तर, शंका लागेका र आरोप खेपेकामाथिको अनुसन्धान हघि बढ्दा यसको प्रभावकारितामाथिका चासोहरु बढेका छन् ।

अख्तियार दुरुपयोग अनुसन्धान आयोगले दुईजना पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्रीहरुका स्वकीय सचिव र पूर्वपरराष्ट्रमन्त्री आरजु राणा देउवाका पूर्वसहयोगीमाथि अनुसन्धान अघि बढाएको छ । अख्तियारले पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री शेरबहादुर देउवाका स्वकिय सचिव भानु देउवा र पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री प्रचण्डकी छोरी समेत रहेकी स्वकिय सचिव गंगा दाहालविरुद्ध अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ ।

यतिमात्रै नभई अख्तियारले पूर्वपरराष्ट्रमन्त्री तथा देउवा पत्नी आरजु राणा देउवाका सहयोगी समेत रहेका सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशसभाका सदस्य प्रकाश बहादुर देउवामाथि पनि अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ। जसमध्ये प्रकाश अहिले पनि अमेरिकामै रहेका छन्। प्रकाश आरजुको निकट सहयोगी रहेको बताइन्छ भने उनी २०७९ मा सम्पन्न प्रदेशसभा निर्वाचनमा कैलाली क्षेत्र नम्बर–५ (२) बाट प्रदेश सभामा निर्वाचित भएका थिए । उनी २०७९ माघमा प्रदेशको भौतिक पूर्वाधार विकास मन्त्री बनेका थिए । प्रकाश र भानु दुबै देउवाका भतिजहरु हुन्।

अनुसन्धान जारी

अख्तियारले तीनजनाविरुद्ध नै सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरण र भ्रष्टाचारसम्बन्धि कसुरमा अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको बताइन्छ। प्रकाशविरुद्ध पूर्वमन्त्री समेत भइसकेकाले भ्रष्टाचार र सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरण र गंगा र भानुविरुद्ध भने सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरणको अनुसन्धान चलिरहेको अख्तियारले जनाएको छ ।

प्रकाश देउवाविरुद्धको अनुसन्धान कसरी ?

प्रकाश देउवा अहिले अमेरिकामा छन्। उपचारका लागि भन्दै अमेरिका पुगेका प्रकाश अहिलेसम्म नेपाल फर्किएका छैनन्। उनी प्रदेश सांसद समेत भएपनि लामो समय संसदमा अनुपस्थित रहँदै आएका छन्। धेरैले उनको सेवा सुविधा नै कटौति हुनुपर्ने माग गरिरहेको बेला प्रदेश संसद सचिवालयले यसबारे थप बुझ्ने काम भइरहेकोबाहेक जवाफ दिने गरेको देखिन्न। भने तलव रोक्का गर्ने प्रावधान नै नरहेको भन्ने गरेको छ। यता, अख्तियारले पनि प्रकाश अमेरिकामा भएकोबाहेक सूचना प्राप्त गर्न सकेको देखिन्न। उनीविरुद्ध अख्तियारले अनुसन्धानका निम्ति फारम भराउने गरि तयारी गरिरहेको बताइन्छ ।

भानु देउवा र गंगा दाहालविरुद्ध के हुँदैछ ?

भानु र गंगाबारे अनुसन्धान गर्न सम्पत्ति शुद्धीकरण अनुसन्धान विभागले पत्राचार गरेको अख्तियारले जनाएको छ। एकहप्ताअघि मात्रै सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरणको पत्र प्राप्त गरेको अख्तियारको दाबी छ। योसंगै अख्तियारले विभिन्न विभागमा उनीहरुको सम्पत्ति विवरण माग गर्दै पत्राचार समेत गरिसकेको बताइएको छ। सम्पत्ति विवरण संकलनपश्चात मात्रै उनीहरुलाई सम्पत्ति सम्बन्धि फारम भराउने र बयान लिने काम थाल्ने अख्तियारको जिकिर छ । यता, अख्तियारका अधिकारीहरुले उनीहरुको बैंक विवरण र कारोबारको विवरण एकीकृत गरिरहेको समेत बताइन्छ।

केपी ओलीका स्वकियविरुद्ध पनि अनुसन्धान

अख्तियारले पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री केपी ओलीका स्वकिय राजेश बज्राचार्यविरुद्ध अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ। गएको जेठ अन्तिम सातादेखि अनुसन्धान शुरु गरेको अख्तियारले के गरिरहेको छ भन्ने प्रगति विवरण सार्वजनिक रुपमा दिने गरेको छैन् ।

बज्राचार्यले अकुत सम्पत्ति आर्जन गरेको आरोपमा अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको अख्तियारले उनलाई फारम भराउनेदेखि बयान लिने काम समेत गरिसकेको बताइन्छ। बज्राचार्यले सम्पत्ति विवरण सम्बन्धी १३ पन्ने फारम भरेर अख्तियारमा बुझाइ सकेका छन् । बज्राचार्यविरुद्ध यति समूहको थामसेर्कु ट्रेकिङले दरबारमार्गस्थित नेपाल ट्रस्टको जग्गा लिजमा लैजादा अनियमितता गरेको आरोप छ। बज्राचार्यकी पत्नी रश्मि शाक्यले यति समूहबाट बालकोटस्थित रोज भिलेज हाउजिङभित्रको झण्डै चार आना जग्गामा बनेको घर घुस बापत लिएको केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्यूरो (सीआईबी)को अनुसन्धानको निष्कर्ष छ । यहि विवरण देखाउदै सीआइबीले नै अख्तियारलाई लेखि पठाएपछि अनुसन्धान अघि बढिरहेको छ । उसोतः सम्पत्ति विवरणमाथि अनुसन्धान गर्दा गैरकानुनी रूपमा आर्जन गरेको भेटिएमा आयोगले भ्रष्टाचार निवारण ऐन २०५९ अनुसार विशेष अदालतमा मुद्दा दायर गर्न सक्ने कानुनी व्यवस्था छ । अहिले आयोगले गरिरहेको अनुसन्धानको निष्कर्षपछि मात्रै अभियोजन हुने नहुने विषय टुंगो लाग्नेछ।

अख्तियारमाथि भरोसा कि प्रश्न ?

अख्तियारले गरिरहेका अनुसन्धान र अभियोजन कति प्रतिशत अदालतबाट प्रमाणित हुन्छन्? पछिल्लो समय यो प्रश्न उठिरहेको छ। अख्तियारले अभियोजनलाई कर्मकाण्डी बनाउने गरेको आरोप समेत लाग्ने गरेको छ। यस्तोमा अख्तियारले अभियोजनका लागि समय लिएपनि परिपक्क अनुसन्धान गर्नुपर्ने र अभियोजनमा समेत विशेष ध्यान दिनुपर्ने बताइन्छ। तर, अख्तियारमाथि कार्यपालिकाको हस्तक्षेपका कारण पनि अनुसन्धान प्रभावकारी हुनेमा शंका भने देखिन्छ। तर, अख्तियारले आफ्नो शाख जोगाउने र गैरकानूनी सम्पत्ति आर्जन र भ्रष्टाचार नियन्त्रणमा उल्लेख्य भूमिका खेल्नुपर्ने संवैधानिक व्यवस्थाको पालना कसरी गर्छ भन्ने प्रश्न र भरोसा कायमै देखिन्छ।

articles.title: याडियाका तीन नयाँ स्मार्ट विद्युतीय स्कुटर नेपाली बजारमा, १० हजार छुटको अफर
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपालका लागि याडिया (YADEA) को आधिकारिक वितरक कुजु नेपाल प्रा. लि. ले नयाँ पुस्ताका GS70, GT70 र GTM90 विद्युतीय स्कुटरहरू नेपाली बजारमा औपचारिक रूपमा सार्वजनिक गरेको छ। आधुनिक प्रविधि, उत्कृष्ट कार्यक्षमता र नेपाली सडक अनुकूल डिजाइन गरिएका यी स्कुटरहरूले दैनिक सहरी यात्रादेखि लामो दूरीको यात्रासम्मका फरक-फरक आवश्यकता पूरा गर्ने कम्पनीको भनाइ छ।

सार्वजनिक गरिएका तीन मोडेलमध्ये GS70 लाई दैनिक सहरी यात्राका लागि किफायती विकल्पका रूपमा तयार पारिएको छ। यसमा २.१ kWh LFP ब्याट्री र २.८ kW पिक मोटर दिइएको छ, जसले एकपटकको पूर्ण चार्जमा १०५ किलोमिटरसम्मको रेन्ज प्रदान गर्छ। लामो दूरीको यात्रा गर्नेहरूका लागि GT70 उपयुक्त छ, जसमा ५.७ kWh को डुअल LFP ब्याट्री (३.६ kWh फिक्स्ड र २.१ kWh रिमुभेबल) तथा ३.७ kW पिक मोटर रहेको छ। यसले २२० किलोमिटरसम्मको रेन्ज दिन्छ भने रिमुभेबल ब्याट्रीका कारण घर वा कार्यालयमा सहजै चार्ज गर्न सकिन्छ। प्रिमियम श्रेणीको GTM90 मा ३.६ kWh लिथियम ब्याट्री र ५ kW पिक मोटर जडान गरिएको छ, जसले ८० किमि प्रतिघण्टाको उच्च गति र १५० किलोमिटरसम्मको रेन्ज दिन्छ।

प्रविधि र सुरक्षाका हिसाबले यी नयाँ स्कुटरहरू निकै आधुनिक छन्। ती सबैमा TFT स्मार्ट डिस्प्ले, ब्लुटुथ कनेक्टिभिटी, मोबाइल नेभिगेसन मिररिङ, याडिया स्मार्ट एप, कि-लेस प्रणाली र ५ जनासम्म प्रयोग गर्न मिल्ने 'फ्यामिली सेयरिङ' सुविधा उपलब्ध छ। यात्रालाई थप सुरक्षित र सहज बनाउन ट्र्याक्सन कन्ट्रोल सिस्टम (TCS), क्रुज कन्ट्रोल, हिल होल्ड, हिल डिसेन्ट कन्ट्रोल र डुअल डिस्क ब्रेकजस्ता अत्याधुनिक प्रविधि समावेश गरिएका छन्।

कम्पनीले तीनै मोडेलका ब्याट्रीमा ३ वर्ष वा ५०,००० किलोमिटरसम्मको दीर्घकालीन वारेन्टी प्रदान गरेको छ। हाल यी स्कुटरहरू देशभर रहेका २० वटा आधिकारिक याडिया डिलरशिपहरू मार्फत उपलब्ध छन्। साथै, सार्वजनिक गरिएको अवसरमा नाइमा अटो शो (NAIMA Auto Show) सम्म लागू हुने गरी कम्पनीले तीनै मोडेलमा रु. १०,००० को विशेष नगद छुट दिएको छ। ग्राहकहरूले नजिकैको शोरुममा गई टेस्ट राइड तथा फाइनान्सिङ सुविधाबारे थप जानकारी लिन सक्नेछन्।

articles.title: खल्तीबाट डिजिटल भुक्तानी गर्दा दैनिक १ लाख र बम्परमा १० लाख जित्न सकिने
articles.summary:
काठमाडौँ । आईएमई खल्ती लिमिटेडले अर्थ मन्त्रालयअन्तर्गतको आन्तरिक राजस्व विभागद्वारा सञ्चालित ‘करदाता प्रोत्साहन उपहार कार्यक्रम, २०८३’ मा आफ्ना प्रयोगकर्तालाई सहभागी गराउने भएको छ। खल्तीमार्फत रु १०० भन्दा बढीको योग्य डिजिटल भुक्तानी गर्दा ग्राहकहरू स्वतः दैनिक तथा पाक्षिक उपहार छनोटमा सहभागी हुनेछन्।

यस कार्यक्रमअन्तर्गत दैनिक एक जना विजेताले कर कट्टीपछि रु. १ लाख र प्रत्येक १५ दिनमा एक जना बम्पर विजेताले रु १० लाख प्राप्त गर्नेछन्। भुक्तानीको विवरण सुरक्षित रूपमा राजस्व विभागको प्रणालीमा पुग्ने र उपहार कुपन स्वतः सिर्जना भई खल्ती एपमै देखिने व्यवस्था मिलाइएको छ। विभागले प्रत्येक महिनाको १ र १६ गते स्वचालित प्रणालीबाट विजेता छनोट गरी एसएमएस, इमेल तथा खल्तीमार्फत जानकारी गराउनेछ।

बिलमा आधारित कारोबार प्रवर्द्धन गरी डिजिटल अर्थतन्त्र र राष्ट्रिय राजस्व प्रणालीलाई सुदृढ बनाउने लक्ष्यका साथ यो सहकार्य गरिएको आईएमई खल्तीका प्रमुख कार्यकारी अधिकृत प्रवीण रेग्मीले बताएका छन्।

articles.title: सर्वसाधारणको रकम गरिमा विकास बैंकले झ्वाम पार्दै, झ्वाम पार्ने को–को ?
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । के तपाईंको गरिमा विकास बैंकमा खाता छ ?के तपाईंले आफुले मेहेनत गरेको रकम गरिमा बिकास बैंकमा राख्नु भएको छ ? यदी छ भने तपाईंका लागि आज दुखको खबर छ । कारण हो, ग्राहकले राखेको रकम बैंकको भवन किन्दा अपचलन गरेर प्रचलित मूल्यभन्दा बढी मूल्यामा किनिएको छ । प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कन प्रतिवेदन र प्रचलित बजार मूल्यलाई समेत लत्याउँदै बैंक व्यवस्थापनले ३५ करोड ४० लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी मूल्य तिरेको छ । सर्वसाधारणले दुःख गरेर बैंकमा जम्मा गरेको निक्षेप सुरक्षित छ त?भन्ने प्रश्न पनि उठिरहेको छ ।

गरिमा विकास बैंकले काठमाडौँको बालुवाटारमा ३७ आनाभन्दा बढी जग्गा र त्यसमा बनेको घर खरिद गर्दा प्रचलित बजार मूल्य र स्वयं प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कन प्रतिवेदनलाई समेत लत्याउँदै करिब ३५ करोड ४० लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी मूल्य तिरिएको भेटिएको छ। बजार मन्दीमा रहेका बेला प्राविधिक प्रतिवेदन भन्दा दोब्बर मूल्य हालेर जग्गा र भवन किनिएको छ ।

काठमाडौंको बालुवाटारमा कित्ता नम्बर ४९ मा रहेको २ रोपनी ५ आना १ पैसा अर्थात् ३७ दशमलव २६ आना जग्गा र ४७ हजार ६ सय २१ वर्गफिटको बनेको यो आरसीसी भवन शिखर इन्स्योरेन्सका पूर्वअध्यक्ष राजेन्द्रप्रसाद श्रेष्ठको २०८२ सालमा गरिमा विकास बैंकले केन्द्रीय कार्यालय बनाउन खरिद ग¥यो ।

बैंकले यो जग्गा खरिद गर्दा प्रतिआना १ करोड ५६ लाख १४ हजार ९२२ रुपैयाँ तिरेको देखिन्छ । अर्थात २ रोपनी ५ आना १ पैसाको जग्गाको मूल्या ५८ करोड १८ लाख १२ हजार रुपैयाँ बैकलाई पर्न गयो। अब यही जग्गामा रहेको यो भवनको क्षेत्रफल ४७ हजार ६ सय २१ वर्गफिट रहेको छ ।

बैंकले यो भवनको मूल्य ३९ करोड ३१ लाख ८८ हजार रुपैयाँमा खरिद गरेको देखिन्छ । वर्गफिटमा हिसाब गर्दा पनि प्रति वर्गफिट ८ हजार २ सय ५६ रुपैयाँमा खरिद गरको छ । तपाईलाई यो खरिद मूल्य सायद सामान्य नै लाग्यो होला? यो सामान्य घरजग्गा किनबेच देखिए तापनि, प्राविधिक प्रतिवेदन र बैंकको हालेको रकम जुधाउँदा भने ठूलो अन्तर देखिन्छ ।

प्राविधिक प्रतिवेदन र बजार मूल्यको वास्तविकता

पृथक इन्जिनियरिङ कन्सल्टेन्ट्सले बैंक धितोकै लागि तयार पारेको प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कन प्रतिवेदन अनुसार सो क्षेत्रमा जग्गाको स्थानीय बजार दर प्रतिआना ८० लाख रुपैयाँ मात्र छ। स्थानीय व्यवसायीहरूका अनुसार पनि बजारको अधिकतम मूल्य ९० लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी पर्दैन।

प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कन प्रतिवेदनमा सडकको अधिकार क्षेत्र कट्टा गरी कायम भएको १ रोपनी १३ आना ३ पैसा जग्गाको कुल बजार मूल्य १७ करोड ७० लाख ९८ हजार मात्रै कायम गरेको छ । पृथक इन्जिनियरिङ कन्सल्टेन्ट्सले कमर्सियल भ्यालु अनुसार मूल्याङ्कनको निष्कर्ष भनेको २३ करोड ८३ लाख ९९ हजार यो जग्गाको मूल्या कायम गरेको छ । फेयर मार्केट भ्यालु अनुसार मूल्याङ्कनको निष्कर्ष भनेको १७ करोड ७० लाख ९८ हजार कायम गर्यो ।

डिस्ट्रेस भ्यालु अनुसार मूल्याङ्कनको निष्कर्ष भने १४ करोड १६ लाख ७८ हजार कन्सल्टेन्ट्सले कायम गरेको छ । तर बंैकले बैंकले भने सोही जग्गालाई ५८ करोड १८ लाखभन्दा बढी भुक्तानी गर्यो। यो खेल जग्गामा मात्र रोकिएन, भवन खरिदमा पनि उस्तै अस्वाभाविक मूल्या हालियो ।

४७ हजार ६ सय २१ वर्गफिट क्षेत्रफल रहेको सो भवनको मूल्य बैंकले ३९ करोड ३१ लाख ८८ हजार रुपैयाँ तय गरेर खरिद ग¥यो। अर्थात् प्रतिवर्गफिट ८ हजार २ सय ५६ रुपैयाँ! निर्माण व्यवसायीहरूका अनुसार काठमाडौँमा अत्यन्त लक्जरियस सामग्री प्रयोग गर्दा पनि नयाँ भवन निर्माण खर्च प्रतिवर्गफिट अधिकतम ४ हजारदेखि ६ हजार रुपैयाँसम्म मात्र पुग्छ। प्रतिवर्गफिट ६ हजार नै मान्ने हो भने पनि २८ करोड ५७ लाख पर्ने भवनलाई बैंकले १० करोड ७४ लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी अतिरिक्त मूल्य हालेर किनेको देखिन्छ ।

जग्गामा २४ करोड ६५ लाख र घरमा १० करोड ७४ लाख गरी कुल ३५ करोड ४० लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी रकम बजार मूल्य र प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कनभन्दा बढी मूल्य हालिएको छ । घर–जग्गा बजारमा मन्दी छाएका बेला प्रचलित भाउभन्दा निकै माथि गएर गरिएको यो निर्णयमा गरिमा विकास बैंकका सञ्चालक अनिल रेग्मी, ईश्वरीप्रसाद ढकाल र सीईओ माधवप्रसाद उपाध्याय लगायतको भूमिका देखिन्छ ।

सर्वसाधारण निक्षेपकर्ताको पसिनाको कमाईमाथि बैंकका सञ्चालक र उच्च व्यवस्थापनबाट भएको यो अस्वाभाविक खर्चले बैंकको संस्थागत सुशासन र नियमनकारी निकाय नेपाल राष्ट्र बैंकको अनुगमनमाथि ठूलो प्रश्न खडा गरेको छ।

articles.title: फोनिज काठमाडौँको आयोजनामा वृक्षरोपण तथा पदयात्रा सम्पन्न
articles.summary:
काठमाडौँ । नेपाल आदिवासी जनजाति पत्रकार महासंघ (फोनिज) काठमाडौँ जिल्ला कार्यसमितिको आयोजनामा वृक्षरोपण तथा फोनिज पदयात्रा सम्पन्न भएको छ ।

फोनिजको २७ औँ स्थापना दिवसको अवसर पारेर आज शनिवार काठमाडौँको साँखु–बज्रयोगिनी हुँदै मणिचूड दहसम्म पदयात्रा तथा विभिन्न गुम्बा तथा मन्दिर परिसरमा वृक्षरोपण गरेका हुन् । काठमाडौँ जिल्ला अन्तरगत फोनिज आवद्ध प्रतिनिधिहरू, स्थानीय जनप्रतिनिधि र विभिन्न जातिय संघसंस्थाका प्रतिनिधिहरूको उल्लेख्य सहभागितामा साँखुमा भेला भइ बज्रयोगिनी मन्दिर परिसरबाट करिव १७ किलोमिटिरको दूरीमा पदयात्रा गरेका थिए ।

पदयात्रापछि मणिचूड दहमा भएको औपचारिक कार्यक्रममा विभिन्न वक्ताहरूले धार्मिक पर्यटन प्रवद्र्धन र संरक्षणमा आदिवासी जनजातिहरूको महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका रहेको बताएका छन् । कार्यक्रममा बोल्दै शंकरापुर नगरपालिका वडा नं. ८ का अध्यक्ष पोते थिङले मणिचूड दहको महत्वबारे प्रकाश पार्दै प्रचारप्रसारको अभाव तथा राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्ज वन क्षेत्रको निश्चित मापदण्डका कारण अझै ओझेलमा परेको बताए । मणिचूड दह र त्यस क्षेत्रमा रहेका हरेक धार्मिक तथा साँस्कृतिक सम्पदाको संरक्षण र प्रवद्र्धनका साथै थप व्यवस्थापन गर्न वनसंग जोडिएको कानुनलाई परिमार्जण गर्नुपर्ने धारणा राखे ।

त्यस्तै शिवपुरी नागार्जुन राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्ज मध्यवर्ती क्षेत्र व्यवस्थापन समितिका अध्यक्ष श्यामकुमार वाइबाले निकुञ्जभित्र रहेको मणिचूड दह बौद्ध र हिन्दू दुवै धर्मालम्बीहरू पवित्र तिर्थस्थलको रूपमा मान्दै आएको बताए । विशेष गरि जनजातिजातिको बहुल्यता रहेको त्यस क्षेत्रमा बौद्ध धर्मालम्बीहरूले विभिन्न समयमा पूजापाठ, मोन्लाम लगायत साउन महिने जलयात्रा, जनैपूर्णिमा लगायत साँस्कृतिक पर्वहरू मनाउने भएकोले थप महत्व रहेको बताए । अहिले निकुञ्ज, स्थानीय तह र मन्दिर व्यवस्थापन समितिबीचको समन्वयमा व्यवस्थित बनाउने रणनीति रहेको बताए ।

कार्यक्रममा राष्ट्रि शहिद तथा शान्ति स्मारक पार्क र गोकर्ण यज्ञडोल सामुदायिक वन उपभोक्त समितिका अध्यक्ष सुर्दशन सिग्देलले वन, जंगल, जल र जमिनको संरक्षणमा जनजाति समुदायको उल्लेख्य भूमिका रहेको बताउँदै आफ्नो साँस्कृतिक पहिचान र अधिकारसँग जाडिएको क्षेत्रमा राज्यले दुःख दिन नहुने बताए । जनजाति समुदायले विशेष गरि प्रकृतिको पुजा गर्ने चाडपर्वलाई साँस्कृतिक पहिचानको रूपमा विश्वमाझ चिनाउन सफल रहेको बताउँदै राष्ट्रिय शहिद पार्क वन क्षेत्रमा समेत विभन्नि जातजातिको अस्तित्व समेट्ने गरि भिलेजग्रामको निर्माण गरिएको बताए ।

फोनिज बागमति प्रदेश समितिका महासचिव राजु नापितले फोनिजले पत्रकारितालाई आफ्नो पेसागत हकअधिकारमात्र नभएर भाषा, कला, संस्कृतिको संरक्षण र सम्वद्र्धनमा विशेष योगदान पु¥याउँदै आइरहेको बताए । फोनिज बागमति प्रदेशभित्र पत्रकारहरूलाई एकीकृत गराउँदै समुदायको पहिचान र अधिकार सुनिश्चित गराउन समेत जिल्लासमितिहरूले सक्रियतापूर्वक गतिविधि सञ्चालन गराउँदै आएको बताए ।

त्यस्तै फोनिज संघीय समितिका सचिव सुनिल महर्जनले फोनिज पदयात्राले रमाइलो मात्र नभइ अनुसन्धानका आयाम बुझ्न पाएको बताए । मणिचूडको सुन्दर ऐतिहासिक धार्मिक पर्यटकीय स्थल प्रकृतिप्रेमी र आध्यात्मिक शान्ति चाहनेहरूका लागि विशेष रहने बताउँदै पत्रकारिताको माध्यमबाट प्रचारप्रसारलाई तिब्रता दिनुपर्ने बताए । फोनिजले नेपालभित्र रहेका आदिवासी जनजाति समुदायसंग जोडिएका कला, भाषा, धर्म संस्कृति र पहिचान बोकेका विषयवस्तुहरूको अध्ययन र अनुसन्धान गरि विश्वसामु चिनाउने प्रयास गरिरहेको बताए ।

नेपाल आदिवासी जनजाति पत्रकार महासंघ (फोनिज) काठमाडौँ जिल्ला समितिका अध्यक्ष भिमबहादुर लामाले सामाजिक एकता र सद्भाव कायम उद्देश्यका साथ फोनिजको २७ औँ स्थापना दिवसलाई सार्थक पार्न पदयात्रा तथा वृक्षरोपण कार्यक्रमको आयोजना गरिएको बताए । उनले जनजाति पत्रकारहरूको पेसागत क्षमतालाई दरिलो बनाउन अध्ययन, अनुसन्धान र आलेख लेखनमा सहयोग पु¥याउने उद्देश्यले धार्मिक पर्यटकीय क्षेत्र तथा जनजाति समुदायको साँस्कृतिक तथा धार्मिक महत्व बोकेको क्षेत्र साँखु, बज्रयोगिनी र मणिचूड दहको यात्रा तय गरेको बताए । राज्य र पहुँचवाला समूहहरूबाट आदिवासी जनजातिहरूको थातथालोमा जलविद्युत गुरूयोजनाहरू सञ्चालन गर्ने, विकास निर्माण र राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्जको नाममा परिवारहरू विस्थापित बनाएको अध्यक्ष लामाले आरोप लगाए ।

फोनिज काठमाडौँ जिल्ला कार्यसमितिका सचिव रत्नमान महर्जनले सञ्चालन गरेको कार्यक्रममा नेपाल प्रहरीका पूर्व डिआइजी देउती गुरूङ, गोकर्णेश्वर नगरपालिका वडा नं. ८ का वडा सदस्य सुमन लामा, नेपाल पत्रकार महासंघ काठमाडौँ शाखा उपाध्यक्षद्वाय कमल राना मगर, कान्ति न्यौपाने, सहसचिब बिक्रम रत्न, मणिचूड मन्दिर व्यवस्थापन समितिका अध्यक्ष भिम घ्लान, नेपाल बौद्ध धर्म संरक्षण संघका महासचिव उमा गुरूङ, साँस्कृतिक युवा समूहका अध्यक्ष वेचन लामा, समाजसेवी किरण मोक्तान, सोफिया पाख्रिन लगायत अतिथि रहेका थिए । पदयात्रामा फोनिजकर्मी तथा विभिन्न संघसंस्थाका प्रतिनिधि गरि ६८ जनाको सहभागीता रहेको थियो ।

articles.title: Deuba faction’s Hindu line opens new fault line in Nepali Congress
articles.summary:
“I am a Hindu, I am a Hindu, I am a Hindu.”

Former prime minister Sher Bahadur Deuba, who returned to Nepal last Thursday after spending nearly five months abroad, made the emphatic statement at the closing ceremony of a three-day national gathering organised by a faction of the Nepali Congress in Sukedhara on Sunday.

He further said that his personal faith did not mean he opposed other religions or rejected Nepal’s religious freedom.

“And I have love and reverence for Buddha and Buddhism. The world today recognises Buddhism. Today, Buddhism is also referred to as a scientific religion and is regarded as such. Likewise, ours is a country that respects nature-based religions. The Rai and Limbu communities follow nature-based religions, and we must respect all of them. I respect them.”

The Deuba faction’s decision to promote Sanatan religion as a national identity has opened a new ideological fault line in the Nepali Congress, while its rejection of Gagan Thapa’s leadership threatens to deepen the party’s organisational dispute.

The three-day gathering concluded on Sunday with a five-point declaration that commits the party to promoting Sanatan religion as a national identity while pledging to protect Hindu, Buddhist, Kirat and nature-based faiths and the religious freedom of all communities.

But the religious provision was added at the last minute and was absent from the 20-point conclusion prepared for the gathering, according to Congress leaders.

The earlier document described Nepal as a multi-ethnic, multilingual, multi-religious and multicultural country and guaranteed communities the freedom to practise and preserve their faiths and cultures.

Bimalendra Nidhi’s political proposal also made no mention of promoting Sanatan religion as a national identity or supporting a Hindu state. The gathering was initially expected to endorse the 20-point conclusion.

After Deuba reviewed the proposal, however, a separate five-point declaration was prepared under his direction, a Congress leader said. It recognised Nepal’s traditional religious and cultural heritage as part of its national identity and committed the party to promoting Sanatan religion while protecting Hindu, Buddhist, Kirat and nature-based faiths and religious freedom.

The move faced resistance within the Deuba camp. Nidhi objected to the new declaration, which was absent from his proposal, and exchanged words with Prakash Sharan Mahat on the stage, according to Congress leaders. The five-point declaration was nevertheless read out and endorsed by the gathering.

Political analysts say the move marks a departure from the party’s position since the 2015 Constitution, which defines Nepal as a secular state. They see it as an attempt to establish a distinct political identity after losing control to Thapa.

“The decision to adopt the Hindu line may have been driven by Deuba’s search for political and personal security,” said Krishna Khanal, a political analyst. “Otherwise, religion—whether Hinduism or secularism—does not appear to have been an issue that mattered much to him as a leader.”

Khanal said Deuba’s decision should not necessarily be read as the result of a long-developed political philosophy. “There may have been an influence of Hindu extremists in India,” he said. “The thinking could be that taking this line would make politics and security easier. I do not see it coming from a long-term ideological view of Nepal. Personally, I do not think Deuba makes much distinction between secularism and Hinduism.”

The issue has been present in Congress for years. At the party’s Mahasamiti meeting in February 2024, more than 1,000 members signed a petition calling for Nepal to be restored as a Hindu state. The campaign was led by lawmaker Shankar Bhandari, but Deuba, who was party president at the time, did not formally endorse the demand.

This time, the Deuba camp has gone further by formally adopting Sanatan religion as a national identity. The declaration says Nepal’s longstanding religious and cultural traditions are part of its national identity and commits the party to preserving Hindu, Buddhist, Kirat and nature-based religions while ensuring religious freedom, tolerance and social harmony.

Congress leader Prakash Sharan Mahat described the decision as an important departure in the party’s internal politics after the constitution was promulgated. He said support for a Hindu state had existed in Congress forums before, but the party leadership had not formally taken ownership of it.

“Until now, Congress had repeatedly said that secularism was a provision of the constitution,” said Mahat. “This time, we have said that Sanatan religion is a national identity and have adopted this as a policy through the gathering.”

He said the gathering also rejected the social democratic policy advanced by Thapa after the special general convention and returned to BP Koirala’s concept of democratic socialism. “There are two important departures,” said Mahat. “One is the return to democratic socialism, and the other, more important one, is the position on Hindu religion.”

The decision was not without opposition inside the Deuba camp. According to Congress leaders, Nidhi tried to stop the religious provision from being inserted into the declaration because it was absent from the political proposal presented to the gathering. Another senior leader, Krishna Prasad Sitaula, also expressed dissatisfaction.

Nidhi has consistently defended republicanism, federalism and secularism as achievements of the constitution. Sitaula was coordinator of the constitution drafting committee during the constitution-making process. One Congress leader said Bhandari, who has long advocated a Hindu state and constitutional monarchy, was prevented from speaking at the opening session to avoid creating a Hindu-state atmosphere.

The organisational dispute is even more consequential. The Deuba faction has rejected the special general convention held in January and the central committee elected under Thapa. It has declared that the 15th general convention should be organised by the central committee elected through the 14th general convention and held under Deuba’s leadership.

The position directly challenges the Election Commission’s recognition of the Thapa-led Congress in January. The commission had ruled that the special convention was valid because the party statute allows at least 40 percent of general convention representatives to demand such a gathering. It also held that general convention representatives are the party’s supreme authority.

The Supreme Court in April upheld the recognition of the Thapa-led faction, ending the immediate legitimacy dispute. But the Deuba faction filed a review petition in July, bringing the dispute back before the court.

This legal battle has become intertwined with the party’s preparations for its next regular general convention. Congress Vice-President Bishwa Prakash Sharma has argued that rejecting the leadership recognised by both the Election Commission and the Supreme Court risks further dividing the party.

“A decision made at a programme attended by Deuba himself amounts to contempt of court,” said Sharma. “The court’s decision to grant permission for review did not make Deuba the party president. Going beyond what the court has said and calling him president is contempt.”

The Deuba faction, however, argues that Congress should not proceed with organisational activities while the leadership dispute remains before the Supreme Court. NP Saud said holding a general convention while the review petition is pending could affect the final outcome of the case and amount to contempt of court.

“If the party continues towards the convention by ignoring the Supreme Court’s order on the review, that would amount to contempt,” said Saud. “No action should be taken that could adversely affect the pending case related to the Congress dispute.”

The Thapa camp has taken the opposite view, saying the party cannot indefinitely delay its regular convention because of the court case. Sharma said the existing schedule for the central convention should remain in place, although lower-level schedules could be adjusted by the central committee.

The dispute comes after a dramatic year for Congress. Thapa and Sharma called the special general convention after more than half of the elected representatives demanded it. The Deuba camp boycotted the gathering, but the convention elected Thapa president and a new central committee. The Election Commission then recognised the new leadership.

The party’s crisis has also been worsened by its poor performance in the March elections. Congress won only 38 seats, down sharply from the 89 seats it had secured in the 2022 election. Thapa later resigned as party president, taking responsibility for the electoral defeat, but the central committee rejected his resignation.

The latest Hindu identity decision therefore comes at a particularly unsettled moment. For Deuba’s supporters, it offers a way to preserve their political space and appeal to traditional voters. For critics, it risks weakening Congress’s commitment to the constitutional order and widening the ideological gap with Thapa’s reform-oriented camp.

“While the party’s decisions are under discussion, it is not appropriate to comment on such matters,” Sharma said. “But anything adopted by the gathering that strengthens the organisation and serves Congress, democracy and the country will not be viewed negatively. We will discuss how such matters can be incorporated.”

articles.title: Nepal’s faith is finding a new interface
articles.summary:
For centuries, religious knowledge in Nepal has travelled through priests, scriptures and oral traditions. Increasingly, it is also travelling through smartphones.

A growing group of Nepali developers is building apps and devices that put rituals, mantras, astrology and religious texts on demand, betting that technology can make practices rooted in centuries-old traditions fit more easily into modern life.

The market is still small. But the experiments are multiplying.

Five years ago, Nabin Khatiwada and Yubaraj Dhungel, two Sanskrit students from eastern Nepal who studied in Vrindavan, India, started with an unusually simple idea: put a Hindu ritual book on a phone.

Their project, Brihat Karmakanda, has since evolved into a business. The app now offers digital religious texts and horoscope readings, has over 50,000 downloads and attracts over 37,000 monthly active users.

Its newest paid feature suggests where the business may be heading.

Nearly 500 people subscribed to its horoscope service within days of its launch. Annual membership costs Rs299, while five-year and 50-year plans cost Rs999 and Rs2,999 respectively.

“We started by digitising a book,” Khatiwada said. “Then we realised there was much more we could do.”

The path from Sanskrit text to software was not straightforward. Khatiwada initially struggled with the technical requirements for publishing an app, including obtaining a dollar card to pay Google Play Store fees. After the developer helping him left following the release of Android 13, he taught himself coding and backend programming.

Today, the two-person operation is split between technology and text. Khatiwada handles programming; Dhungel prepares and types Sanskrit material.

The app initially relied on Google advertising for revenue. Paid astrology has opened another stream, and Khatiwada plans to add artificial intelligence to the platform.

Brihat Karmakanda is one small example of a broader shift: religious practice is beginning to acquire the logic of a technology product.

The same impulse is visible in hardware.

Pokhara-based Yarsa Labs has built a battery-powered “chanting box” that plays mantras and devotional songs for a set period. Founder NJ Subedi said the company developed the device after noticing that people often play music during morning and evening prayers.

Designed like a mirror and decorated with Hindu deities and traditional motifs, the device turns a familiar ritual accompaniment into a consumer product.

“We have not actively marketed the technology, but we make it when there is demand,” Subedi said.

Technology is also entering Nepal’s religious heritage sites, although in a different form.

Bikash Gurung, president of the Nepal Robotics Association, points to a robotic attraction at a Buddhist monastery in Lumbini that has been operating since around 2013. At the Buddha Gram Robotic Live Museum, robotic and animatronic figures recreate episodes from the Buddha’s life, from his birth and renunciation to enlightenment and death.

Gurung sees possibilities beyond museums and attractions.

“Automating some processes at monasteries, temples and cultural sites listed as heritage sites could make things easier,” he said. “It would not necessarily interfere with traditional practices.”

The bigger commercial opportunity, however, may lie in astrology.

Subedi considers astrology the strongest market for faith technology in Nepal, pointing to Hamro Patro’s service that connects users with astrologers by phone. Other Nepali platforms, including Bihebari, use technology to match couples based on horoscopes, gotras and nadi compatibility. Nepali developers have also experimented with building AI chatbots such as Prithvi AI and Jyotish AI around astrology and religious guidance.

“There is a sizeable market for faith tech in Nepal,” Subedi said.

What has held the sector back, he argues, is not necessarily demand but attitudes toward monetising religion.

“Our society is not as comfortable with making money from people’s faith,” he said. “So Nepal has not seen as many faith-tech apps as India.”

India offers a glimpse of what that market could become.

There, astrology, spirituality and religious practice have already spawned a substantial digital economy. AstroTalk, AstroSage AI and Astrosure.ai are among the platforms competing for users seeking everything from horoscope readings to spiritual advice.

AstroTalk, launched in 2017, now has more than 70 million users and over 18,000 astrologers, reported journalist Bhuvana Kamath for The Economic Times. Kamath has reported that the platform accounts for about 80 per cent of India’s online astrology market.

Meanwhile, Astrosure.ai has created a chatbot named Agastya to offer horoscope analysis and mental health advice, drawing around 1.8 million monthly active users.

Other products push the idea further, using generative AI to simulate conversations with religious figures or offer AI-guided spiritual assistance, including platforms like Gita GPT, Quran GPT, and Vedas AI.

Gita GPT, developed by Vikas Sahu using GPT-3.5 technology, lets users ask questions in separate chat rooms modelled on 11 religious figures, including Krishna, Ram, Shiva, Hanuman, Buddha, and Chanakya. The service is available in 16 languages, including Nepali.

Other platforms, such as Devaseva and Sri Mandir, aim for religious services themselves, offering virtual worship (e-darshan), delivery of prasad, and virtual participation in Vedic rituals.

The appeal is particularly strong among younger users.

A survey of 500,000 users by Indian faith-tech company Astroyogi found that most users of digital spiritual services were aged 25 to 35, with Gen Z accounting for a significant share. Some 53.8 percent of Gen Z respondents said they turned to astrology for answers about life and the world.

Their questions were not confined to traditional religious concerns. Love and relationships, careers, positive energy and “energy cleansing” were among their main interests.

Users were also willing to pay. The survey found that Indian consumers paid between IRs150 and IRs1,999 per consultation for spiritual guidance and counselling.

For Nepali developers, that points to both an opportunity and a question.

The technology is already available. The demand appears to exist. What remains uncertain is how far people will allow software, algorithms and machines to mediate practices that have traditionally depended on priests, astrologers and personal faith.

For now, Nepal’s faith-tech industry is still experimenting.

But the experiments suggest that the next priest, astrologer or religious guide may not always be waiting in a temple or sitting across a desk. Sometimes, they may be inside a phone.

articles.title: Landslides pile on the misery in Jajarkot settlements
articles.summary:
Kedar Karki, a resident from Jajarkot, one of the remotest areas in western Nepal, survived the devastating 6.4 magnitude earthquake three years ago.

Following the earthquake, Karki’s family of seven spent nearly two years inside a flimsy temporary shelter. A month ago, driven out by relentless monsoon rains, they ventured back into their half-ruined mud-and-stone house.

When a massive landslide struck the settlement on Saturday evening, the rickety house turned into a deadly trap. Kedar, 52, sustained severe injuries in the landslide and died en route to a hospital in Nepalgunj.

The disaster highlights an escalating crisis across Jajarkot, where extreme weather is battering fragile communities still reeling from the earthquake.

“This landslide has devastated our entire village, causing huge human casualties and physical destruction,” said Bhim Bahadur Karki, ward chair of Bheri Municipality-2. The landslide has killed four and left six people injured, all of whom are currently undergoing treatment at the district hospital.

Nearly 90 percent of the 300 households in Risang were already affected by the 2023 earthquake. The recent landslides have damaged the majority of surviving structures across Paldanda, Chyaumuda, Chisapani, Neta, and Jhyalkhet, according to the ward chief.

Alongside Karki, search teams recovered the bodies of Om Singh Khatri, his mother Rati Khatri, and Bhim Bahadur Karki, on Sunday morning after they went missing on Saturday night.

Local authorities face a daunting rescue effort amid widespread infrastructure destruction.

“Landslides have occurred in almost every single neighbourhood, making it impossible to move from one cluster to another,” said ward chief Karki. “The area is entirely shattered, and it is impossible to assess everyone’s status right now.”

Displaced residents are currently taking shelter at various community buildings.

The District Disaster Management Committee, the Nepal Red Cross Society and Bheri Municipality have provided tarpaulins, tents, utensils and emergency food supplies such as beaten rice, instant noodles and biscuits for the displaced.

“We have distributed non-food items from the supplies available with the committee and by coordinating with non-governmental organisations,” said Chief District Officer Khadananda Adhikari. “The municipality has arranged dry food, including instant noodles and biscuits, for the displaced families.”

Local community leader Dhan Bahadur Karki said the displaced families were in a desperate situation. “None of us has been able to eat a proper meal,” he said. “We neither had enough to eat nor could we sleep properly yesterday. A single tarpaulin has been distributed to each family, but the rain has continued. We have been forced to stay awake again today.”

Deputy Superintendent of Police Buddhi Sagar Puri said that approximately 150 people remain trapped in various isolated locations across the ward.

Security forces, including 200 personnel from the Nepali Army, Armed Police Force and Nepal Police, have been deployed for search and rescue operations.

Several quake-hit settlements in Jajarkot are at high risk of landslides. According to the District Disaster Management Committee in Jajarkot, 68 earthquake-affected settlements in the district are at high danger of landslides.

“The earthquake had already cracked the surrounding terrain,” said Chief District Officer Khadananda Adhikari. “The tremors weakened the land’s initial structure, and continuous rains exacerbated the instability, leading to further destruction.”

Adhikari stated that rescue teams evacuated 16 people from Jhyalikhet, 20 from Chisapani, 15 from Rauterata Danda, and three from Pharula to safer ground.

According to the District Disaster Management Committee, settlements severely damaged by the earthquake—including Sagachaur, Libal, and Detkule in Chhedagad; Laikham in Barekot; Chaur, Chaupani, and Maide in Bheri Municipality; Dungara, Luppakha, and Bhius in Shivalaya; and Chiuri and Pali in Nalgad—are also at high risk of landslides.

Displacements are mounting rapidly in Junichande Rural Municipality-3 as well. The authorities relocated 12 families from Syala due to the landslide threat.

Thousands of earthquake survivors were forced to construct temporary huts on high-risk slopes, riverbanks, and edge-of-cliff farmlands. Geologists had previously warned that post-earthquake landscapes suffer up to an 80 percent higher risk of landslides due to deep structural fractures in the soil.

“Earthquakes shake the rock formations and loosen the topsoil, creating wide fissures,” said geologist Santosh Sharma. “Consequently, even brief rain showers or minor shocks can cause entire hillsides to give way.”

The water-induced disasters wreak havoc in the quake-affected settlement each monsoon season. On July 13, 71-year-old Jasi Kumari Shahi died and three others were injured inside a temporary hut in Bheri Municipality–2. Eight people perished in Jajarkot landslides last year alongside seven individuals in neighbouring Rukum West.

For survivors, the disaster compounds years of administrative neglect and delayed rebuilding support. “Before the pain of the earthquake could even heal, these landslides have destroyed our remaining homes,” said Ramesh Karki, a local teacher at Tribhuvan Basic School. “Without permanent housing, we were already living painful lives in temporary huts. The rain has not stopped, risks are rising, and displaced families are sitting here hungry.”

Despite 48,517 beneficiaries being identified in Jajarkot and 34,954 temporary shelters erected, Chief District Officer Adhikari admitted that formal reconstruction work has yet to begin.

The devastating earthquake, with its epicentre in Ramidanda of Barekot Rural Municipality, killed 154 people and damaged around 76,000 houses across Jajarkot and Rukum West. Thousands of earthquake-displaced families continue to live in temporary shelters or quake damaged houses due to the delay in reconstruction and rehabilitation of the victims. The quake victims are exposed to threats from landslides and floods during monsoon while they are left shivering under flimsy huts in winter.

articles.title: Commercial banks post 32 percent profit surge despite weak credit demand
articles.summary:
Nepal’s commercial banks recorded a 32 percent increase year-on-year in net profit in the last fiscal year, despite weak economic activity, sluggish credit demand and a sharp rise in excess liquidity in the banking system.

According to unaudited financial statements published by the country’s 20 commercial banks, their combined net profit rose to Rs69.78 billion in the fiscal year ended mid-July, from Rs52.79 billion a year earlier.

Bankers say the increase was driven largely by stronger loan recoveries in the fourth quarter, which allowed banks to reverse some impairment charges and reduce provisioning for potential loan losses.

The rise in profits comes as the wider economy continues to face weak demand. For the third consecutive year, banks have been holding large amounts of excess liquidity, private-sector credit demand has remained subdued, domestic industries have been operating at only around 42 percent of capacity, and the prolonged crisis in the cooperative sector has weighed on consumption.

Santosh Koirala, president of the Nepal Bankers’ Association, said the increase in profits did not reflect a significant expansion in lending.

“Loan disbursement showed negligible improvement over the fiscal year, resulting in only marginal gains in net interest income,” Koirala said. “The bottom-line growth is almost entirely driven by notable recoveries of bad loans.”

He said the improvement in loan recovery could indicate a gradual revival in real estate transactions and a greater willingness among borrowers to repay their debts.

The improvement, however, was uneven across the banking sector. Sixteen of the 20 commercial banks reported higher profits. Himalayan Bank recorded the largest percentage increase, with its profit rising by more than 1,100 percent from a low base. Three banks reported lower profits, while Prabhu Bank posted a net loss.

In terms of absolute profit, Nabil Bank was the largest earner, with a net profit of Rs7.90 billion, up 33 percent from Rs5.92 billion a year earlier. Kumari Bank followed with Rs7.38 billion, Global IME Bank with Rs6.22 billion and Everest Bank with Rs5.06 billion.

NIC Asia Bank reported the smallest profit, at Rs180 million, but this represented a recovery from a loss of Rs3.87 billion in the previous fiscal year.

Bank executives and analysts caution that the increase in profits does not necessarily signal a broad-based recovery in the banking sector.

Sudesh Khaling, chief executive officer of Everest Bank, said regulatory concessions introduced by Nepal Rastra Bank, including loan restructuring and rescheduling in selected sectors, had also supported banks’ balance sheets.

“While loan recovery improved for several large institutions, lowering provisioning write-offs, liquidity remains heavily trapped in the banking system while fresh credit demand is virtually absent,” Khaling said. “Banks cannot sustain profit growth over the long term unless underlying economic fundamentals improve.”

Despite stronger recoveries in the final quarter, the sector’s asset quality deteriorated. The average ratio of non-performing loans (NPL) rose to 5.35 percent at the end of the fiscal year 2025-26, from 4.51 percent a year earlier.

Five commercial banks reported NPL ratios above 7 percent. Prabhu Bank had the highest ratio at 15.55 percent, while Everest Bank had the lowest among the banks, at 0.49 percent.

At the same time, banks’ total provisioning for bad loans fell to Rs37.30 billion by July 17, from Rs44.69 billion a year earlier. The reduction in provisioning helped lift banks’ reported profits.

Net interest income, a key source of earnings for banks, increased by just 1 percent to Rs192.35 billion in the last fiscal year, from Rs189.84 billion a year earlier, reflecting the limited growth in lending.

Four banks ended the fiscal year with negative distributable profits, while 16 recorded positive distributable profits. Based on their net profits, banks had an average dividend capacity of 13.42 percent.

Banks also transferred Rs4.82 billion to regulatory reserves in the fourth quarter because of uncollected interest, in line with Nepal Rastra Bank rules requiring 51 percent coverage.

The sector’s average earnings per share increased to Rs19.96 from Rs16.42 a year earlier.

Bhuwan Dahal, former president of the Nepal Bankers’ Association, said the results showed a widening gap in the performance of individual banks rather than a uniform recovery across the sector.

“The fourth-quarter financial statements present a mixed picture. Banks that managed their portfolios prudently showed strong indicators across credit flow, recovery, and non-performing loans,” Dahal said. “However, several institutions saw no credit growth, poor recoveries, and elevated loan-loss provisions, causing their distributable profits to shrink.”

At the broader economic level, the financial and insurance sector is projected to grow by 9.16 percent in the fiscal year 2025-26, according to the National Statistics Office. The projected growth is 1.61 percentage points higher than in the previous fiscal year.

The NSO attributed the growth to increases in bank deposits and loan disbursements, as well as higher renewals of life and non-life insurance policies. It also cited increased value addition from the Social Security Fund, Employees Provident Fund, Citizen Investment Trust, stock market transactions and merchant banking activities.

The NSO revised its estimate for financial and insurance sector growth in the fiscal year 2024-25 to 7.55 percent, compared with 9.96 percent in the fiscal year 2023-24.

Despite the projected increase in output, the sector’s contribution to Nepal’s gross domestic product fell slightly to 6.72 percent in the last fiscal year from 6.78 percent a year earlier.

Meanwhile, nearly Rs1.5 trillion in excess liquidity was sitting in the banking system by mid-July. Steady remittance inflows, combined with weak domestic demand for loans, resulted in loanable funds accumulating throughout the fiscal year.

The large pool of idle funds, despite the increase in bank profits, underscores the disconnect between the financial sector’s earnings and broader economic recovery. Banks have more money available to lend, but businesses and households have remained reluctant or unable to borrow at the scale needed to drive a stronger expansion in economic activity.

articles.title: Nepal revives industrial security force to restore investor confidence
articles.summary:
In September 2012, Nepal government decided to establish an Industrial Security Force to provide security to industrial firms, particularly those operating in industrial zones.

The decision was taken after a rise in kidnappings, killings, threats and extortion targeting industrialists and businessmen by armed gangs in the post-conflict period.

At the time, militant labour organisations also posed a threat to the smooth operation of factories and industrial firms.

In early 2020, the government removed the permanent presence of Armed Police Force personnel deployed under the Industrial Security Force from several industrial areas. The personnel were redirected to border areas following concerns over the spread of the coronavirus along the borders and across the country.

They were never redeployed.

Again, in September last year, the Gen Z movement caused massive damage to industrial establishments and businesses across the country, with losses estimated at more than Rs84 billion.

The rise in vandalism, looting, arson and theft has discouraged potential new investors, while existing businesses have been compelled to operate in fear.

On July 30, protesters in Golbazar, Siraha, vandalised and set fire to several shops, including AB Mall, before security forces moved in.

The new government led by Balendra Shah has now revived the Industrial Security Force concept.

Last Friday, Nepal launched the Private Investment Protection and Promotion Strategy, which envisions establishing an Industrial Security Force to protect the physical assets of industrial and business establishments.

The strategy also calls for formulating a new industrial policy to guarantee industrial and business security.

Before the launch of the strategy, Prime Minister Shah held a marathon meeting with representatives of small and large businesses and industrialists.

Officials say that under the strategy, industrial corridors, industrial areas, special economic zones and industrial villages will be declared peace zones, with arrangements made to prevent any form of undesirable activity in industrial establishments.

“The strategy has been prepared and implemented following the damage caused to private-sector businesses during last September’s Gen Z movement,” said Netra Prasad Subedi, joint secretary at the Ministry of Industry. “The action strategies include protecting and promoting industries and businesses and attracting investment. Besides, the recent Tarai movement has also caused damage to businesses.”

The ministry has requested the relevant ministries and other government agencies to implement the strategy accordingly, he said.

“There are challenges to protecting private-sector properties,” Subedi added. “We have the strategy now to protect them. This is the beginning.”

The private sector’s morale remains low. According to a World Bank report, private investment has been weighed down by weaker investor confidence following the September 2025 unrest.

The report said private investment remained almost stagnant, expanding by just 0.2 percent in the last fiscal year 2025-26.

Weak investment reflects persistent weaknesses in the overall business environment, policy uncertainty and continuing challenges in channeling available liquidity into productive investment, according to the report.

The private sector, which contributes roughly 81.55 percent of overall national output and drives more than 86 percent of employment creation, however, remains unconvinced.

“We are the first target every time,” said Kamlesh Kumar Agrawal, president of the Nepal Chamber of Commerce. “The latest is the Tarai protest… We still can’t be fully certain that the incident will not repeat in the future.”

The Shah administration has set an ambitious target of expanding the national economy to nearly $100 billion and raising per capita income to $3,000 within five to seven years, while targeting average annual economic growth of 7 percent.

“Without taking the private sector into confidence, this is not possible,” said Agrawal, adding that the strategy is welcome and incorporates suggestions made by the private sector. “If there is anything lacking, it can be reviewed.”

To improve the industrial and business environment and increase investment, the government has made timely amendments to laws including the Industrial Enterprises Act, Foreign Investment and Technology Transfer Act, Companies Act, Special Economic Zone Act, and Public-Private Partnership and Investment Act, among others.

But effective implementation of these measures remains questionable, amid declining industrial capacity utilisation and a falling contribution of industry to GDP.

Manoj Paudel, founder and chairperson of Aadhyanta Fund Management, a Kathmandu-based private equity and venture capital firm, said the private sector has been targeted by protests for several decades, but there is no single instance in which the government has protected businesses or assured them that such incidents will not recur.

“Where is the action against the wrongdoers?” he said. “There is no single record.”

He said the introduction of the strategy was a starting point, but its implementation would determine its effectiveness in restoring the confidence of industries and businesses.

“The private sector needs the sense of security that if their business gets vandalised, the state will take strong action against it,” he said.

Adopting a zero-tolerance policy against attacks, vandalism and arson targeting the physical assets and businesses of industrial and business establishments is one of the strategies outlined in the government document.

The strategy provides for classifying industrial and business establishments according to their security risks and providing security accordingly. It also calls for mobilising quick-response or rapid-response teams based on the risk of damage to industries, businesses and private property.

The strategy also provides for designating a security focal or contact person at the nearest security unit to address the security needs of industries and businesses.

It provides for waiving applicable fees, penalties and fines, as allowed under prevailing laws and the annual budget and programmes, for industries, businesses, firms and companies that have not been renewed for a long time. The waiver would apply when they update their records, renew their registration, submit required details or deregister within a specified period.

The government also plans to amend environmental regulations and other prevailing laws to allow privately owned industrial and business structures damaged during protests or other movements to be relocated to new sites by requiring only an Initial Environmental Examination.

The government says it has formulated the Private Investment Protection and Promotion Strategy to encourage the private sector to invest with greater confidence and maintain an environment of trust, with the aim of accelerating economic development, attracting investment and generating employment.

A coordination and facilitation committee comprising government and private-sector representatives will be formed to ensure effective implementation of the strategy.

Implementation will be monitored by the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers and the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies.

articles.title: Monsoon disasters demand more than rescue
articles.summary:
Nepal’s monsoon disasters are becoming a grim annual occurrence. Over the past four months, more than 80 people have died in monsoon-related disasters; nine are missing, and 196 have been injured. On Saturday, three people lost their lives in separate landslides in Jajarkot and Rolpa districts, and last week, a mudslide buried a settlement in Rolpa, leaving 10 dead and three missing. Unfortunately, as we are only halfway through the monsoon season, there is a high risk that the death toll will continue to mount. This alarming situation warrants greater seriousness from the government.

Successive governments have consistently failed to prevent the high number of deaths and destruction caused by the monsoon-related disasters. Their aversion to preventing haphazard road construction in different parts of the country has only increased the vulnerability of Nepal’s precarious hill landscape. In many rural hill districts, roads are still built without proper surveys. Local authorities, to meet targets and avoid a budget freeze, often resort to asare bikas, without regard for the dangers of landslides, deaths and displacement. Once constructed, roads are left without proper maintenance and upgrades.

The absence of guidelines about where people can safely build houses in remote hilly areas has also put many lives at risk. At the same time, unregulated riverbed and hill mining has intensified the impact of monsoon-related disasters. For example, in 2024, the Roshi river flood in Kavrepalanchok district killed 78 people, partly due to illegal mining and unregulated crusher industries. Often, these activities occur because of political backing and contract manipulation, yet they operate freely.

In April, Home Minister Sudan Gurung ordered the immediate shutdown of illegal crusher plants after visiting a flood-affected area in Kavrepalanchok district. The Balendra Shah-led government also decided to manage the resources needed to prevent and respond to monsoon-related disasters. Following monsoon disasters, hundreds of rescuers have also been deployed in the affected areas. These steps are welcome but far from enough. Nepal cannot stop the monsoon, nor can it prevent every landslide and flood. But it can mitigate the human costs of predictable disasters.

Shifting the focus from how quickly rescuers reach disaster-affected areas to whether people receive early warnings and whether they trust and act on them is necessary. Equally vital is holding people accountable for haphazard road construction and illegal mining. The public, too, must follow disaster-related early warnings and avoid building homes in risky zones. In Rolpa alone, over 100 households need immediate relocation. Local governments must immediately transfer such vulnerable settlements to safe places and coordinate with the provincial and federal government if necessary. Urgent action is also needed in 134 settlements across all nine local units of Bajura district. In Jajarkot, 200 people who were at risk have been relocated, which is a much-needed step.

The government aimed for zero deaths in monsoon-related disasters this year. Instead, authorities have recorded 85 deaths so far. These deaths must only push the government to acknowledge the fact that it fell short in adequately focusing on prevention before disasters struck. Rather than treating monsoon-related destruction and deaths as an annual ritual like past governments did, it should treat them as a year-round governance challenge and prioritise prevention, early action and preparedness. The government must identify where the risks lie before more disasters and deaths expose them.

articles.title: The overlooked impact of inadequate rainfall and fertiliser shortages in Nepal’s agriculture sector
articles.summary:
Two Nepali farmers from the Sarlahi district were released on bail from an Indian jail on August 7 after spending 38 days in custody for allegedly ‘smuggling’ fertiliser from India. They had crossed the border to buy fertiliser for their paddy fields: a routine practice in border areas where residents regularly purchase essential goods, including agricultural inputs, from across the frontier whenever domestic supplies run short.

Driven by desperation to secure enough fertiliser for their annual staple crop, their experience reveals the plight of thousands of Nepali farmers who, ahead of every planting season in May–June, anxiously track two things: the skies, hoping for timely and adequate rain, and government depots, waiting for fertiliser. For far too long, uncertainty on both fronts has disappointed them. Inadequate rainfall and unreliable fertiliser supplies remain two of the most critical and overlooked constraints in Nepal’s agriculture sector, despite successive governments’ plans and policies claiming to prioritise agriculture in public spending.

Nuances often overlooked

As debates over Nepal’s declining food production continue in academic circles and policy corridors, the practical nuances that keep the agricultural system functioning are often overlooked. The case of these two farmers has brought one of the most critical of these nuances into sharp focus: the heavy reliance on cross-border sources of agricultural inputs. Unlike in previous years, when small quantities of fertiliser for personal use were generally permitted, Indian authorities have now adopted a stricter approach. This tighter enforcement may not be coincidental; it follows Nepal’s own stricter customs measures, which impose duties on merchandise valued above Rs500 (previously Rs100) entering from India, which has impacted Indian border markets dependent on Nepali customers. These developments have introduced a degree of strain into bilateral relations, affecting communities on both sides of the border.

When domestic fertiliser supplies run short, farmers in the Tarai region are often constrained to buy from markets across the border. That desperate measure proved costly for these two men, who not only spent more than five weeks in jail but also faced sharply reduced harvests this year for lack of fertiliser. Their ordeal highlights deeper weaknesses in Nepali agriculture: the persistent uncertainty of fertiliser availability just before the main planting season, a problem successive governments did not address effectively; the desperation that pushes farmers to seek inputs wherever they can; and the way shifting relations with neighbouring countries shape the daily lives, livelihoods and local economies of communities that depend on cross-border trade.

Loss of food production, for whatever reason, be it lack of inputs, disasters or diseases and pests, is not merely a farmers’ issue; it is a national concern of immense gravity affecting us all. Any problem farmers face anywhere in the country signals a shortcoming in our agricultural pursuit and must be addressed accordingly. For instance, dry spells in the middle of the monsoon, once rare exceptions limited to a few areas, have become routine. In 2022, farmers in western Nepal were forced to abandon their newly planted crops and move across the border to earn a living after a prolonged dry spell. In 2026, farmers in Salyan and Banke districts couldn’t plant paddy due to inadequate rain. Likewise, delayed monsoon rains in October damaged ready-to-harvest paddy across large swaths in both 2021 and 2025.

These and other similar episodes have long sent clear distress signals calling for meaningful, ground-level support. Yet, we have consistently failed to interpret them correctly or respond with the required urgency. Consequently, agriculture has gradually lost its appeal, driving many farmers to abandon farming in favour of the labour market.

Rising food deficit

The state’s prolonged failure to answer these calls is starkly reflected in Nepal’s relentlessly rising food import bill, which has doubled over the past eight years. In the last fiscal year alone, the country imported food worth Rs434.26 billion, making food its second-largest external dependency after petroleum products. The issue is not so much the volume of imports itself, because every country imports food at some scale. The difference lies in the nature of that dependence.

Many of the world’s largest food-importing nations are also among the wealthiest. However, when a country like Nepal imports food to meet basic sustenance needs, the resulting external dependence becomes a serious vulnerability, especially when a significant share of national income comes from remittances, which currently account for over a quarter of GDP—the highest among countries in the region. Imported food cannot secure long-term resilience; the only sustainable path to limit import bills is to strengthen local production.

In the face of mounting climate challenges, our failure over the decades to address nuances in agriculture is likely to cost us more than we may presume. The United Nations has warned that the rapidly developing El Niño weather system is likely to push about 50 million people globally into acute hunger before the end of 2027, in addition to the hundreds of millions already facing dangerous levels of food insecurity. South and Southeast Asia are likely to get less rainfall than usual, causing serious problems for agriculture. This foreboding should serve as a critical reminder that this fast-approaching crisis will be far greater than any we have faced before. How will we manage the El Niño fallout when we haven't even been able to ensure a reliable supply of fertilisers?

Governance challenge

The current government is committed to taking strict measures to improve governance, yet the pace at which these changes are being pushed through feels abrupt. Any reform is bound to fail if the system is not prepared to absorb it. Deep-rooted mismanagement, however unacceptable, cannot be undone overnight. Existing systems have long adapted to involve complex linkages across different layers of society; these interdependencies must be carefully considered when addressing governance, particularly in cross-border markets and their linkages with agriculture that feeds the nation.

Understanding these interdependent connections is essential before attempting broader governance reforms. Effective improvement requires a clear grasp of the lives of those at the lowest rungs of society, particularly the lives of the thousands who till the soil to make a living. This will not happen without practical measures that address the full range of underlying issues. Addressing them requires understanding social norms, policies and institutions formed deep in history. Those details determine whether policies work or fail.

As long as those who plough the fields and grow our food end up in jail while following ordinary practices, or are driven across the border when drought ruins their harvest, we cannot claim to be acting in the true interests of the citizens in whose name we seek better governance. Meaningful change must begin from the bottom, not the top. Otherwise, corrective measures risk harming those most in need of support and protection, causing them to lose faith in the very government they elected with a supermajority.

articles.title: How Nepali diaspora literature confronts borders and belonging
articles.summary:
The invitation I received early this month from the Centre for Nepal Studies UK to participate in a live webinar on the topic ‘How does diaspora writing reshape the Nepali literary sphere?’ impressed me in several ways. Nepali diaspora writing has strongly drawn the attention of researchers, Nepali writers and literary critics over the years. Literary writers and critics have been eloquent on this subject.
